Resolves #21375

🌿 Tearing out a window's center pane can no longer leave that window as a strip in its corner.

Demo B's main window keeps its center as a place while the center pane is away. `LayoutAdapter`'s opt-in `enableDockCenterWell` projects an edge-zone with an empty center as a well. The well takes the center's `flex: 1`, so the band keeps its edge at full height, and it names the away pane from the TearOut's recorded homes ("Workbench is in its own window"). When the vessel closes, `Operations.centerWellReturnDescriptor`, Demo B's new return policy, rebuilds the center from its captured home: the round trip is the identity. Hosts without the option are unchanged. The well as a drop target is #21827.

Evidence: L3 (the headed matrix arm on macOS Chrome, plus the frames below) → L3 required (AC-2, AC-3, AC-4).

| AC-2 | Outside-CI: `TearOutMatrixRows4To7NL.spec.mjs` row 7, headed (`playwright.config.matrix.mjs`): after the drop, the band and the well refill the area the panes covered, and the well reads "Workbench is in its own window". CI-covered: `DockLayoutAdapter.spec.mjs` "the center well (#21375)". |
| AC-3 | Outside-CI: the same arm, after the vessel closes: the panes refill, no well remains, and `root.zones.center` holds `['workbench']`. CI-covered: `DockZoneModel.spec.mjs` "centerWellReturnDescriptor" (the round trip equals the source document). |
| AC-4 | The row 7 arm runs without `test.fail` and passes: the whole spec, 5 of 5 arms, headed on macOS Chrome, on this head's code (a later amend changed comments only). The unit arms cover the rebuild from `captureNodeHome`, and a control arm pins the band landing of the append policy that this fixes. |

## Deltas from ticket

- **The well is opt-in, not the engine default.** Hosts project centerless edge-zones on purpose (the Workstation's empty window workspace, `apps/workstation/view/Workspace.mjs:196`), so a default change the night before the cut would move surfaces this ticket keeps out of scope.
- **The return rule is its own policy.** `centerWellReturnDescriptor` treats a still-free edge-zone center as a surviving home and delegates everything else to `appendingReturnDescriptor`, which the Workstation keeps using unchanged.
- **`TearOut#getProjectionCallbacks` also hands over `dockAwayPlacements`**, the live record of recorded homes, so a well can name its pane in any TearOut host.
- **The drop target is #21827.** It needs a new placement kind across the producer, the preview contract, the renderer and the indicators.

Row 5, row 7 committed, refill, post-birth cancel and blocked acquisition all pass, so the new return policy leaves the other terminals as they were.

Frame critique:
- The band keeps its edge at full height in both themes, and the well's inset hairline and its line read on each ground.
- In neo-dark the well shows the window's own background, a step darker than the band's panel surface: the quiet surface the design read asks for. Clio's look read passes in both themes, nothing to change ([comment](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/pull/21830#issuecomment-7069524813)).
- After the return, the counter reads "3 render-target mounts · same worker instance": the live pane came home rather than a rebuilt copy.
- The well is not a drop target yet (#21827).
